attribution.note: Zitron states and endorses this assessment in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the majority qualifier, product-market-fit clause and qualified valuation judgment. Predominant unprofitability is a firm historical observation.

contract.note: Testing whether most relevant companies had net losses in reporting periods applicable to publication is an ordinary reading. The contract appropriately avoids scoring the qualified valuation judgment or inventing a product-market-fit threshold.

evidence.note: The pre-cutoff company filing discloses a relevant 2024 net loss. It establishes one loss-making company, without establishing the population or prevalence of losses. Later financial periods do not test the June 2025 observation.

The dated report describes a potentially relevant profitable exception during the historical period. Its accounting definition and population membership are uncertain; one exception cannot contradict predominant unprofitability.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes neither a defined company population nor comparable net-income results for enough companies to determine a majority. Anthropic's disclosed loss and Surge's reported profitability do not settle the claim. The qualified valuation judgment and unmeasured product-market-fit language cannot independently resolve it.
